n8e353f3d818.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Mirat-i-Sikandari?
o: It describes the prosperity of Mahmud Begada's kingdom.
It describes the administrative arrangements of Mahmud Begada.
It was written by Sikandar bin Muhammad.
It is a Persian history of the Bengal Sultanate.
n8e353f3d818.x: The Mirat-i-Sikandari by Sikandar bin Muhammad is a Persian history of the Gujarat Sultanate, not Bengal; it describes Mahmud Begada's prosperity and administration.

nb3f9595df44.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Bahmani Sultanate?
o: Muhammad Shah I shifted the capital from Gulbarga to Bidar.
Control of the Raichur Doab was the main cause of its conflict with Vijayanagara.
Ahmad Shah I shifted the capital to Bidar.
Muhammad Shah I built the Gulbarga Jama Masjid.
nb3f9595df44.x: Ahmad Shah I, not Muhammad Shah I, shifted the capital to Bidar; Muhammad Shah I built the Gulbarga Jama Masjid.

n97c7df3e292.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Qutb Shahi revenue apart from land revenue?
o: Taxes on courtesans and professions were a source of revenue.
Compulsory military service replaced all taxes.
n97c7df3e292.x: Trade taxes, port customs and taxes on courtesans and professions supplemented land revenue; military service did not replace taxes.

nindian-history-68-9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the founding of capitals?
o: Ajatashatru established Pataliputra as a fortified settlement.
Udayin shifted the capital from Rajagriha to Pataliputra.
Firoz Shah Tughlaq established Tughlaqabad in Delhi.
Udayin was the successor of Ajatashatru.
nindian-history-68-9.x: Tughlaqabad was established by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, not Firoz Shah Tughlaq; Ajatashatru fortified Pataliputra and his successor Udayin shifted the capital there.

new.s: Which Sultan of Kashmir was called 'Butshikan' (idol-breaker)?
new.x: Sikandar (1389-1413) was Butshikan: he destroyed temples and imposed jizya. Zain-ul-Abidin (Bud Shah) abolished it.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Zain-ul-Abidin?
o: He was the first to abolish jizya in Kashmir.
He built the Zaina Kadal bridge in Srinagar.
new.x: Butshikan was Sikandar; Zain-ul-Abidin was 'Bud Shah', abolished jizya, banned cow killing and built Zaina Kadal.

new.s: Zaina Lank, the island built by Zain-ul-Abidin, lies in which lake?
new.x: Zain-ul-Abidin built the Zaina Lank island in Wular lake.

new.s: The Atala Masjid at Jaunpur was built by:
new.x: Ibrahim Shah Sharqi built the Atala Masjid; the Lal Darwaza Mosque was built by Bibi Raje.

new.s: The Sharqi kingdom of Jaunpur fell in 1479 to:
new.x: Jaunpur under its last ruler Hussain Shah fell to Bahlul Lodi in 1479.

new.s: Who was the last Sultan of Malwa, known for his romance with Rupmati?
new.x: Baz Bahadur, the last Sultan of Malwa, is remembered for Rupmati; he was defeated by Akbar.

new.s: The Jami Masjid at Mandu, begun by Hoshang Shah, was completed by:
new.x: Hoshang Shah began the Jami Masjid of Mandu and Mahmud Khalji completed it.

new.s: Which Sultan of Gujarat was killed by the Portuguese at Diu in 1537?
new.x: Bahadur Shah (1526-37) annexed Malwa, attacked Chittor, was beaten by Humayun and was killed by the Portuguese at Diu.

new.s: The Imad Shahi dynasty of Berar was founded in 1490 by:
new.x: Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk founded the Imad Shahi state of Berar (1490), with its capital at Ellichpur.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (Sultanate – dynasty) is correctly matched?
new.x: Golconda was ruled by the Qutb Shahis; Bijapur was Adil Shahi, Ahmadnagar Nizam Shahi, Bidar Barid Shahi and Berar Imad Shahi.

new.s: The Faruqi dynasty founded by Malik Raja Faruqi in 1382 ruled:
new.x: The Faruqis ruled Khandesh in the Tapti valley, with their capital at Burhanpur.

new.s: Jodhpur was founded in 1459 by:
new.x: Rao Jodha of the Rathores founded Jodhpur (1459); Rao Bika founded Bikaner.

new.s: Translations of the Mahabharata into Bengali were supported by which Sultan of Bengal?
new.x: Hussain Shah (1493-1519) and his son Nusrat Shah supported Bengali Mahabharata translations.

new.s: The Eklakhi Tomb in Bengal is associated with:
new.x: The Eklakhi Tomb is linked with Jalaluddin Muhammad Shah (1414-31); Sikandar Shah built the Adina Mosque.

new.s: In which year did Akbar annex Bengal?
new.x: Akbar annexed Gujarat in 1572 and Bengal in 1576.

new.s: The chronicle Riyaz-us-Salatin deals with the history of:
new.x: Riyaz-us-Salatin is a history of Bengal; Riyaz-ul-Insha is the collection of Mahmud Gawan's letters.

new.s: The Gulbarga Jama Masjid, compared to the mosque of Cordoba, was built by:
new.x: Muhammad Shah I built the Gulbarga Jama Masjid with a fully covered courtyard.

new.s: Mahmud Gawan was the wazir of which Bahmani Sultan?
new.x: Mahmud Gawan, a Persian (Afaqi), was wazir of Muhammad Shah III, under whom the kingdom reached its greatest extent.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Mahmud Gawan:
1. He took Goa in 1472.
2. His letters are collected in the Riyaz-us-Salatin.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Mahmud Gawan took Goa in 1472; his letters are the Riyaz-ul-Insha, while the Riyaz-us-Salatin is a history of Bengal.

new.s: Which Bahmani Sultan, a scholar-king (1397-1422), led the kingdom at its peak strength?
new.x: Firuz Shah (1397-1422) was a scholar-king under whom the Bahmanis were at peak strength.

new.s: Which Deccan Sultanate was the first to break away from the Bahmani kingdom, in 1489?
new.x: Bijapur broke away first (1489); Golconda was the last to break away (1518) and the last to fall (1687).

new.s: Which of the five Deccan Sultanates stayed out of the battle of Talikota (1565)?
new.x: Four of the five sultanates fought at Talikota; Berar stayed out.

new.s: The Adil Shahi dynasty of Bijapur was founded by:
new.x: Yusuf Adil Shah founded the Adil Shahi state of Bijapur in 1489.

new.s: Which Qutb Shahi ruler wrote under the pen name 'Zillullah'?
new.x: Zillullah was Muhammad Qutb Shah, who began the Mecca Masjid; Maani was Muhammad Quli.

new.s: The Qutb Shahi cabinet of Wakil, Peshwa and Mir Jumla was created by:
new.x: Jamsheed (1543-50), who took the throne by killing his father, created this cabinet.

new.s: Which Qutb Shahi ruler concluded a treaty with Shivaji in 1677?
new.x: Abul Hasan Tana Shah, the last ruler, made a treaty with Shivaji in 1677.

new.s: Counting from 1512, Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk ruled for how many years?
new.x: Sultan Quli ruled 31 years counted from 1512 (APPSC 2023).

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Abdullah Qutb Shah:
1. He had the longest reign among the Qutb Shahis.
2. Kshetrayya flourished in his reign.
3. He founded Hyderabad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Abdullah had the longest reign and Kshetrayya flourished under him; Hyderabad was founded by Muhammad Quli (1591).

new.s: In Qutb Shahi administration, the Shahbandar was the:
new.x: The Shahbandar was the chief port officer in charge of customs.

new.s: In Qutb Shahi administration, the Kayasthas were:
new.x: Kayasthas were scribes (APPSC G2 2012); auditors were Majumdars, tax farmers Mustajirs, village accountants Kulkarnis.

new.s: Under Abul Hasan, the Golconda kingdom was divided into how many Sarkars?
new.x: Abul Hasan had 37 Sarkars and 517 Parganas; Abdullah had 6 Tarafs.

new.s: Besides city police duties, the Qutb Shahi Kotwal also ran the:
new.x: The Kotwal was in charge of city police and also ran the mint.

new.s: Tax farmers under the Qutb Shahis were called:
new.x: Mustajirs were tax farmers who bid highest for revenue rights; Mukaddams were village heads and Mahasibs looked after public morals.

new.s: Crown lands under the Qutb Shahis were known as:
new.x: Haveli meant crown lands; Dasabandhu lands paid only one-tenth.

new.s: Which title was held by Madanna?
new.x: Madanna, Mir Jumla/Diwan of Tana Shah, held the title Surya Prakasa Rao; Sar Lashkar was Akkanna's office.

new.s: Madanna and Akkanna were Pingali Brahmin brothers from:
new.x: Madanna and Akkanna were Pingali Brahmins from Hanamkonda who served Abul Hasan Tana Shah.

new.s: The old name of Golconda fort was:
new.x: Golconda's old names were Mankal / Mangalavaram; Bhagyanagar was the original name of Hyderabad.

new.s: The Charminar (1591) was built by:
new.x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah built the Charminar in 1591, when he founded Hyderabad.

new.s: Ibrahim Rauza at Bijapur is the tomb of:
new.x: Ibrahim Rauza is the tomb of Ibrahim Adil Shah II; Gol Gumbaz is the tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah.

new.s: The first European factory in Andhra was set up at Machilipatnam in 1605 by the:
new.x: The Dutch opened the first European factory in Andhra at Machilipatnam in 1605; the English followed in 1611.

new.s: Tavernier, who described the Golconda diamond mines, was a:
new.x: Tavernier was a French jeweller who visited the mines under Abdullah Qutb Shah and wrote Six Travels.

new.s: The Kollur diamond mines lie on the banks of the:
new.x: Kollur, the source of the Kohinoor, is on the Krishna in the Guntur-Palnadu region.

new.s: Golconda diamonds were traded at:
new.x: Diamonds were traded at Moti Darwaza and polished at Karwan.

new.s: Sugriva Vijayam, the first Telugu Yakshagana, was written by:
new.x: Kandukuri Rudrakavi wrote Sugriva Vijayam; Ponnaganti Telaganarya's Yayati Charitra was the first kavya in pure Telugu.

new.s: Who wrote Tapati Samvaranopakhyanamu, the first Telugu kavya dedicated to a Muslim ruler?
new.x: Addanki Gangadhara dedicated Tapati Samvaranopakhyanamu to Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

new.s: Kshetrayya, composer of the Movva padams, flourished under:
new.x: Kshetrayya flourished under Abdullah Qutb Shah; Bhakta Ramadasu belongs to Abul Hasan's time.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Chand Bibi:
1. She was the daughter of Hussain Nizam Shah I.
2. She was the wife of Ibrahim Adil Shah II.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Chand Bibi was Hussain Nizam Shah I's daughter and married Ali Adil Shah; Ibrahim Adil Shah II's wife was Chand Sultana.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Malik Ambar?
o: He was the Abyssinian regent of Ahmadnagar.
new.x: Malik Ambar abolished revenue farming, using survey and fixed assessment on Todar Mal's lines.

new.s: The chronicler Firishta dedicated his work to:
new.x: Firishta dedicated his work to Ibrahim Adil Shah II of Bijapur.

new.s: Abul Hasan Tana Shah, the last Qutb Shahi ruler, was buried at:
new.x: Abul Hasan was imprisoned at Bidar and then Daulatabad, died in 1699 and was buried at Khuldabad.

new.s: After its annexation in 1687, Golconda became which Mughal Suba?
new.x: Golconda became the 21st Mughal Suba.

new.s: Who was the last Nizam Shahi ruler, jailed at Gwalior after 1633?
new.x: Shah Jahan ended the Nizam Shahis in 1633 and jailed the last ruler Husain Shah (Nizam Shah III) at Gwalior; Murtaza III was Shahji's puppet.

new.s: According to the founding legend, the site of Vijayanagara was chosen because there:
o: a cobra shaded a sleeping prince
a hare turned on the royal hunting dogs
a tiger was killed by a boy
new.x: Legend says a hare turned on the royal hunting dogs, so the site was taken as a place of valour.

new.s: Harihara I was crowned on 18 April 1336 at which temple?
new.x: Harihara I was crowned at the Virupaksha temple after Vidyaranya reconverted the brothers.

new.s: The Sangama family claimed descent from which line?
new.x: The Sangamas claimed Yadava (lunar) descent; they are also placed in the Kuruba clan.

new.s: The book 'Kampili and Vijayanagara' was written by:
new.x: Kampili and Vijayanagara is by Nelaturi Venkataramanaiah, not Sewell.

new.s: Which historian did NOT back the Kannada (Hoysala) theory of the origin of Harihara and Bukka?
new.x: Nilakanta Sastri backed the Andhra theory; Heras, Rice and S.K. Ayyangar backed the Kannada/Hoysala theory.

new.s: Under the Kakatiya-service theory, Harihara and Bukka were taken to Delhi and converted after:
new.x: They served Prataparudra of Warangal and were taken to Delhi after 1323.

new.s: The Vijayanagara capital was protected by how many stone ramparts?
new.x: The city had seven stone ramparts and was completed by 1343.

new.s: Harihara and Bukka visited Sringeri after the Hoysala victory in:
new.x: The brothers visited Sringeri in 1346, the year Harihara I annexed the Hoysala kingdom.

new.s: The Aravidu dynasty of Vijayanagara was founded by:
new.x: Tirumala Raya founded the Aravidu dynasty; Vira Narasimha founded the Tuluva dynasty.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a capital of the Aravidu dynasty?
new.x: Aravidu capitals were Penukonda, Chandragiri and Vellore; Anegondi was the first seat of the Sangamas.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Tuluva dynasty:
1. Vira Narasimha is regarded as its founder.
2. Vira Narasimha was crowned in 1505 after executing Immadi Narasimha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Vira Narasimha, son of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka, founded the Tuluva dynasty and was crowned in 1505 after executing Immadi Narasimha.

new.s: Who was the longest-reigning king of the Sangama dynasty?
new.x: Harihara II (1377-1404) was the longest-reigning Sangama king; Devaraya II was the greatest.

new.s: The titles 'Rajavyasa' and 'Rajavalmiki' belonged to:
new.x: Harihara II took the titles Rajavyasa and Rajavalmiki.

new.s: Which Sangama ruler took the title 'Vedamarga Pratishthapaka'?
new.x: Bukka I held the title Vedamarga Pratishthapaka.

new.s: The Italian traveller Nicolo Conti visited Vijayanagara during the reign of:
new.x: Nicolo Conti visited under Devaraya I; Ibn Battuta came under Harihara I.

new.s: Nachana Somana, patronised by the first two Sangama kings, wrote:
new.x: Nachana Somana wrote Uttara Harivamsam and received the Penchikaladinne agrahara.

new.s: Devaraya II's Draksharama inscription (1444) records his success against the:
new.x: The Draksharama inscription records that Devaraya II pushed back the Gajapatis.

new.s: Which Telugu poet was honoured by Devaraya II?
new.x: Devaraya II honoured Srinatha.

new.s: Gangadevi, author of Madhura Vijayam, was a disciple of:
new.x: Gangadevi, wife of Kumara Kampana, was a disciple of Agastya.

new.s: Sayana's Vedic commentary is known as:
new.x: Sayana wrote the Vedartha Prakasha; Mahanataka Sudhanidhi was by Devaraya II.

new.s: Sayana, the Vedic commentator, was the brother of:
new.x: Sayana was Vidyaranya's brother and a minister of Harihara II.

new.s: Saluva Narasimha was the lord of:
new.x: Saluva Narasimha was the lord of Chandragiri; his clan came from Kalyana.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (work – author) is correctly matched?
new.x: Kridabhiramam is by Vinukonda Vallabharaya; Saluvabhyudayam is by Rajanatha Dindima, Jaimini Bharatam by Pinaveerabhadra, Madhura Vijayam by Gangadevi.

new.s: Harihara II gave a daughter in marriage to the son of:
new.x: Harihara II pushed to the Krishna with the Reddis and gave a daughter to Kataya Vema's son.

new.s: Goa was lost by Vijayanagara to the Bahmanis in:
new.x: Goa, taken in 1380 by Harihara II's forces, was lost to the Bahmanis in 1472.

new.s: In the War of the Goldsmith's Daughter, Devaraya I gave which place as dowry?
new.x: Devaraya I gave his daughter to Firuz Shah with Bankapur as dowry.

new.s: The view of Vijayanagara as a 'segmentary state' is associated with:
new.x: Burton Stein described Vijayanagara as a segmentary state in Peasant State and Society in Medieval South India.

new.s: Ferishta's account of the Vijayanagara-Bahmani wars presents the view of the:
new.x: Ferishta was a Persian chronicler who gave the Bahmani view of the wars.
